isolatedDecision.finding: The strongest frame materially improves the lower-body load, chest-height hilt, external blade mass, rear toe skid, and secondary lag. It still fails as one arrested event because both arms advance together, the scapular opposition is weak, the torso remains comparatively quiet, and braid, blade, and boot proportions drift.

visualReview.benchmarkPolicy: Aggregate blinded-comparison results only; no benchmark image, crop, comparison sheet, filename, path, or other benchmark pixel is published.
visualReview.singleBiggestGap: The upper-body force chain is not mechanically arrested: both scapulae and arms still advance as a quiet paired reach, so the upper-right blade mass never resolves through a push-pull shoulder girdle into the ribcage-pelvis C-curve as one violent stop.

engineTruth.finding: The workspace contains an installed editor and a Unity review shell, but no integrated Round011 asset, gameplay controller architecture, encounter scene, or player build. No unrelated shell run or fabricated gameplay capture was filed.

decision.instruction: Preserve the solved lower-body load, toe skid, displaced hilt, and external blade mass; do not begin paid 3D generation or Unity integration from this pack.

conceptArt.finding: The chest-height hilt, external upper-right blade mass, loaded right leg, airborne rear heel, toe skid, and leftward lag read clearly. The quiet paired arm reach and shallow torso deformation prevent one mechanically arrested stop.

builderAttempts.reason: Waist-height near-horizontal hilt, quiet scapulae and ribcage, and insufficient rear-heel lift.
Rear-toe arrest improves, but the centered waist hilt and quiet shoulder girdle still read as a broad held guard.
Torso and weapon share a stronger diagonal, but the rear foot flattens and both elbows remain too similar.
Strongest isolated pose proof, but the fresh critic rejected the paired upper-body reach, shallow C-curve, and identity/design drift.

nextRound.target: Freeze the solved lower-body load, rear toe skid, chest-height hilt, external blade mass, identity, costume, weapon, and framing; re-author only the upper-body force transfer so one scapula drives forward/down, the other retracts/back-up, unequal elbows torque the ribcage against the pelvis, and the blade resolves through a deep C-curve as one violent stop.
